title: The Little Puffin Who Found the Silver Lining
titleZh: 找到一线银光的小海鹦

summary: On Puffin Cliff, far up in the cold northern sea, all the puffins wait a whole year for the Great Sun Festival - the one autumn morning when the sun rises exactly between the two far islands and turns the water to gold. Pim has been counting down for months. But the night before the festival, a thick white sea fog rolls in and does not leave. For three days there is no sun, no sea, and no horizon at all. Old Grumble the seal says the whole year is ruined, and one by one the puffins believe him. Pim keeps finding small good things in the grey - until even Pim's cheer runs thin, and he has to admit, in the dark, that he is disappointed too. Then on the grey festival morning, standing at the edge of the cliff, Pim sees something nobody else has noticed: fog does not only hide things. It also makes them shine.
moral: Pim learned that being cheerful is not the same as pretending nothing is wrong. He was sad about the missing sun, and he said so - and the fog did not go away just because he looked on the bright side. But looking for what was still good did not make the grey day a lie. It just meant he was not alone in it, and that he was still awake when the silver came. You are allowed to be disappointed and still look. Optimism is not saying the rain is not wet. It is saying: the rain is wet, and look how it shines on everything.
moralZh: 皮姆明白了：开心，不等于假装什么事都没发生。太阳没来，他确实难过，他也把这份难过说了出来——而且雾并没有因为「往好处想」就散掉。可在灰色里寻找还剩下的好东西，并不等于自欺欺人；它只是让他没有一个人待在灰里，也让他在银光出现的那一刻还醒着。你可以失望，同时仍然愿意去看。乐观不是硬说雨不湿，而是说：雨是湿的——你看，它把每样东西都擦亮了。

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Far up in the cold northern sea, where the wind smells of salt and the water is the colour of old blue glass, there is a tall green cliff called Puffin Cliff. All summer long the puffins live there in soft grassy burrows, and all summer long they talk about one single morning: the Great Sun Festival. Once every autumn, on one particular morning, the sun rises exactly between the two far islands and the whole sea turns to gold. There is no other morning like it in the entire year.

paragraphs.speaker: Pim
paragraphs.text: (standing at the very edge of the cliff, flapping his little wings) "Three hundred and sixty-four sleeps! I have counted every single one! Tomorrow is the Great Sun Festival!"

paragraphs.speaker: Tilly
paragraphs.text: (a small sandpiper with long quick legs, hopping from stone to stone) "Pim, you count sleeps the way other birds count fish. Do you think the sun will really come right between the islands?"

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: That night, while every puffin on the cliff was dreaming of gold, something quiet came in off the sea. It was not a storm. It was not rain. It was fog - thick, white, patient sea fog, rolling up the cliff like a hundred thousand soft grey blankets, until it swallowed the rocks, and the grass, and the water, and the sky, and the place where the sky and the water meet. In the morning there was no horizon at all.

paragraphs.speaker: Grumble
paragraphs.text: (a big grey seal hauled up on the flat rocks below, his voice like a door creaking) "Well. There it is. There is the whole year, gone. Three hundred and sixty-four sleeps, and the sun cannot be bothered to get up."

paragraphs.speaker: Pim
paragraphs.text: (peering into the white) "It is only fog, Grumble. Fog is just a cloud that came down to visit. It will float off again by lunchtime, you will see."

paragraphs.speaker: Grumble
paragraphs.text: (snorting) "It will not. I have been sitting on this rock for thirty-one years, little bird, and I know a stubborn fog when I smell one. This one has come to stay."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Lunchtime came. The fog did not float off. Evening came, and the fog was still there, soft and white and absolutely everywhere. The next morning it was thicker. A thin cold drizzle began to fall through it, so that everything - feathers, rocks, grass, whiskers - was damp within a minute of waking.

paragraphs.speaker: Pim
paragraphs.text: (sitting on a wet stone, head tilted, listening) "Tilly. Tilly, come here. Stand still and listen."

paragraphs.speaker: Tilly
paragraphs.text: (standing very still, one leg up) "I cannot hear anything at all."

paragraphs.speaker: Pim
paragraphs.text: "Exactly! No wind, no waves crashing, no gulls shouting. The fog has made the whole world quiet. It is like being inside a shell."

paragraphs.speaker: Grumble
paragraphs.text: (from the rocks below) "Quiet is just noise that gave up. And you, little bird, are being silly. Every puffin on this cliff is inside their burrow being miserable, and you are out here being cheerful at a cloud."

paragraphs.speaker: Tilly
paragraphs.text: (quietly, when Grumble had gone back to sleep) "Pim. Why are you always like this? Even when everything is grey, you find something. How do you do it?"

paragraphs.speaker: Pim
paragraphs.text: (a long pause; his wings go still) "I am not always like this, Tilly. I wanted the sun too. I have wanted it for three hundred and sixty-four sleeps."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: That night the fog pressed right up against the burrows, and the drizzle turned the grass to soup. Pim sat outside on the wet rock in the dark, all by himself, and did not say anything cheerful at all. His feathers were damp and flat. His bright striped beak, which usually looked like a painted toy, looked grey in the gloom.

paragraphs.speaker: Pim
paragraphs.text: (very quietly, to nobody) "I wanted to see it turn gold. That is all. I just wanted to see it turn gold."

paragraphs.speaker: Tilly
paragraphs.text: (sitting down beside him, close, without a word at first) "You are allowed to be sad, you know. Being the cheerful one does not mean you are not allowed."

paragraphs.speaker: Pim
paragraphs.text: "I know. I am sad. There. I said it." (a small wet laugh) "It does not make the fog go away, does it?"

paragraphs.speaker: Tilly
paragraphs.text: "No. It does not."

paragraphs.speaker: Pim
paragraphs.text: "Good. Then I will stop pretending it should. But I am not going to sit in my burrow either, because the sun is not the only thing in the world."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Festival morning came, and it was grey. Not stormy, not terrible - just grey, and white, and soft, with the drizzle drifting down and the tide sighing in and out below the cliff. Old Marrow the herring gull stood on the highest stone and looked out at nothing.

paragraphs.speaker: Old Marrow
paragraphs.text: (in his slow, cracked voice) "No sun today. Not one feather of it. The Great Sun Festival will have to wait for next year."

paragraphs.speaker: Grumble
paragraphs.text: "Told you. Thirty-one years I have sat on this rock, and I have never once been wrong about the weather."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: One by one the puffins turned to go back down into their burrows. Pim did not turn. He was standing at the edge of the cliff with his head on one side, the way he did when he was listening to something nobody else could hear.

paragraphs.speaker: Pim
paragraphs.text: (suddenly, loudly) "Wait! Everybody wait! Come and look at the water!"

paragraphs.speaker: Tilly
paragraphs.text: (running back) "Pim, it is just grey water. It is grey water and grey fog and - " (she stops) "...oh."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: The sea was not grey. With no sun to glare on it and no wind to chop it up, the water had gone perfectly flat, and the fog above it was glowing faintly white, and the whole wide sea had turned into one enormous sheet of silver. It stretched away and away until it simply melted into the sky. And every puffin standing on the flat wet rock at the edge of it was reflected in the silver, upside down, beak and all.

paragraphs.speaker: Pim
paragraphs.text: "The sun is not here. I know it is not here. But look what the fog did instead. It took the gold away - and it gave us a mirror."

paragraphs.speaker: Grumble
paragraphs.text: (sliding off his rock and peering into the water, very gruff) "Well." (a pause) "Well. That is... not terrible. That is not terrible at all."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: So instead of a Sun Festival, Puffin Cliff had a Silver Festival. The puffins slid down the wet grass on their bellies and splashed into the shining water. They peeked over the edge of the rocks at their own upside-down faces. They found that in the grey light their orange beaks looked brighter than they ever did in the sun, like little painted lanterns, and they stood in a row on the flat rock just to look at each other.

paragraphs.speaker: Grumble
paragraphs.text: (floating on his back in the silver water, trying very hard not to look happy) "This is the worst festival I have ever attended. I am having a horrible time." (he rolls over and splashes Tilly with his tail) "Absolutely horrible."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: And then, just before noon, a small warm breeze came up off the sea and the fog began to lift. It went slowly, the way fog does, sliding off the water in long soft strips. And when the sun finally got through, low and gold and late, it did not shine on a plain grey sea. It shone on a sea that was already wet and shining and silver, and the whole world lit up twice at once, as if somebody had turned on every lamp in the sky.

paragraphs.speaker: Old Marrow
paragraphs.text: (very softly, watching the light) "There it is. Late. And better than usual, I think." (he turns to Pim) "Little puffin. Come here. I want to tell you the one thing I know about cheerfulness, because most birds get it wrong."

paragraphs.speaker: Pim
paragraphs.text: "What do they get wrong?"

paragraphs.speaker: Old Marrow
paragraphs.text: "They think it means saying the rain is not wet. It does not. The rain is wet. The fog is cold. The sun was late today and you were sad about it, and you were right to be. But you did not go and hide in your burrow and shut your eyes. You stayed out in the grey and kept looking - and so you were the one who was awake when the silver came."

paragraphs.speaker: Tilly
paragraphs.text: (grinning, hopping up beside Pim) "So next year, can we have both festivals? Gold in the morning, silver in the afternoon?"

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Pim laughed, and all the puffins on Puffin Cliff laughed with him, and even Grumble made a noise like a door creaking that everybody decided to count as a laugh. And here is the secret, little one, before you close your eyes. You are allowed to be disappointed. You are allowed to say the day is grey out loud. But do not go and hide in your burrow and shut your eyes - because the silver does not come to the ones who stopped looking. It comes to the ones who stayed out in the weather, still awake, still watching the water. Good night, little one. Sleep well, and keep looking.
